question: Which Mughal ruler had implemented the Manashbari system?  (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Akbar
Humayun
Babar
Darachikoh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
The Mansabdari system was implemented by the Mughal emperor Akbar. It was an administrative and military system where officials were granted a mansab (rank) according to their merit and position. Mansabdars were classified based on Zat (personal rank) and Sawar (number of horsemen). This system was designed to enhance administrative efficiency and military organization. It was developed during Akbar's reign and continued by later Mughal rulers. The Mansabdari system strengthened the central control of the Mughal Empire.

question: Under whose rule was the Charminar monument built in Hyderabad? (RRB ALP Fitter (21/01/2019) Shift 3)

question: Which Mughal Emperor founded Fatehpur Sikri as his capital city? (RRB JE (22/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)
options: Aurangzeb
Babur
Akbar
Humayun
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
The Mughal Emperor Akbar founded Fatehpur Sikri as his capital in 1571 AD. This city is located about 40 km from Agra. Akbar built several architectural marvels here, including the Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, and Birbal's House. Fatehpur Sikri was constructed by Akbar in reverence to the Sufi saint Salim Chishti. Later, in 1585 AD, due to water scarcity, Akbar had to shift the capital to Lahore. Fatehpur Sikri was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986 AD.

question: In Indian history, who was also known as Alamgir? (RRB JE (25/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)
options: Akbar
Jahangir
Aurangzeb
Babur
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Aurangzeb

Explanation:
The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb (1658-1707) was also known by his title 'Alamgir' (Conqueror of the World). He was the sixth ruler of the Mughal Empire and ascended the throne after imprisoning his father Shah Jahan. His reign lasted about 50 years, making it one of the longest in Mughal history. Aurangzeb was an orthodox Muslim ruler who strictly enforced Islamic laws and reinstated the jizya tax on non-Muslims. He expanded the empire into the Deccan and fought against the Maratha ruler Shivaji. His policies eventually weakened the Mughal Empire and contributed to its decline.

question: Where did Muhammad Bin Tughlaq shift his capital to from Delhi?A. DaulatabadB. AurangabadC. AllahabadD. Shaharanpur (RRB NTPC Tier I (16/04/2016) Shift 1)

Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-1351) shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Maharashtra) in 1327, then known as Devagiri. This decision failed due to lack of water and other issues in Daulatabad. Later, he had to shift the capital back to Delhi. This event is considered one of his ill-conceived policies. question: _______ was the 3rd Mughal Emperor of India.A. HumayunB. AkbarC. AurangzebD. Jahangir (RRB NTPC Tier I (19/04/2016) Shift 2)

He was succeeded by Jahangir, Shah Jahan, and Aurangzeb. Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri and patronized the Navaratnas (nine gems) in his court.

question: ______________ is one of India’s largest palaces, which is also known as ‘Amba Villa’ and it was the residence of the Wodeyar monarch.A. Mysore PalaceB. Leh PalaceC. Mattancherry PalaceD. Hampi (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mysore Palace

Explanation:
Mysore Palace, also known as 'Amba Villa', is one of the largest and most famous palaces in India. Located in Mysore, Karnataka, it was the official residence of the Wodeyar dynasty. question: Construction of the Qutub Minar, the world’s tallest brick minaret commenced in 1193, under the orders of ______ the founder of the Delhi Sultanate.A. Firoz Shah Tughlaq.B. Qutub-ud-din Aibak.C. Iltutmish.D. Quli Qutub Shah. (RRB NTPC Tier I (29/04/2016) Shift 2)

Explanation:
The construction of the Qutub Minar, the world's tallest brick minaret, began in 1193 under the orders of Qutub-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Delhi Sultanate. question: In 1857, the last ruler of the Mughal dynasty _______ was overthrown by the British. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/01/2021) Shift 2)

Nasiruddin Humayun

Explanation:
